title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

problem.summary: Region-based detectors such as Fast R-CNN are fast only when the region proposal step is ignored: proposals from Selective Search or EdgeBoxes are computed outside the network, are not shared with the detector, and dominate test-time cost. Multi-scale handling via image or filter pyramids adds further runtime.
statements: External region proposal methods (Selective Search, EdgeBoxes) dominate the runtime of otherwise fast region-based detectors.
Proposal modules are used as external, pre-defined components, so they are not trained end-to-end with the detector and do not benefit from better features.
Addressing multiple object scales and aspect ratios with image pyramids or filter pyramids is time-consuming at test time.

evidence.quote: State-of-the-art object detection networks depend on region proposal algorithms to hypothesize object locations.
Now, proposals are the test-time computational bottleneck in state-of-the-art detection systems.
Nevertheless, the region proposal step still consumes as much running time as the detection network.

The images are resized at multiple scales, and feature maps (HOG [8] or deep convolutional features [9], [1], [2]) are computed for each scale (Figure 1(a)). This way is often useful but is time-consuming.

background.summary: The paper builds on the R-CNN -> SPPnet -> Fast R-CNN lineage of detectors that share convolutions across proposals, and treats Selective Search / EdgeBoxes as the proposal baseline. The claimed gap is that proposals are external modules: MultiBox does not share features with the detector, and R-CNN itself mainly acts as a classifier.

relatedWork.name: Fast R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: second-stage detector that the RPN is merged with and shares convolutional features with
relatedWork.quote: Fast R-CNN [2] enables end-to-end detector training on shared convolutional features and shows compelling accuracy and speed.

relatedWork.name: Selective Search
relatedWork.relation: dominant external proposal baseline, an order of magnitude slower than efficient detection networks
relatedWork.quote: Selective Search [4], one of the most popular methods, greedily merges superpixels based on engineered low-level features.

relatedWork.name: MultiBox
relatedWork.relation: learned proposal network prior work; not fully convolutional and does not share features with the detector
relatedWork.quote: MultiBox does not share features between the proposal and detection networks.

relatedWork.name: OverFeat
relatedWork.relation: prior one-stage sliding-window detector used as the one-stage comparison
relatedWork.quote: In the OverFeat method [9], a fully-connected layer is trained to predict the box coordinates for the localization task that assumes a single object.

evidence.quote: The MultiBox methods [26], [27] generate region proposals from a network whose last fully-connected layer simultaneously predicts multiple class-agnostic boxes
By sharing convolutions at test-time, the marginal cost for computing proposals is small (e.g., 10ms per image).

solution.summary: A fully convolutional Region Proposal Network (RPN) is layered on the shared convolutional feature map and trained end-to-end to predict object bounds and objectness at every location, using a pyramid of anchor boxes as multi-scale regression references. RPN and Fast R-CNN are then merged into one unified network via 4-step alternating training that shares convolutional features.
solution.approach: A small sliding-window network over the shared feature map regresses k anchor-referenced boxes and objectness scores per location, whose proposals then feed the Fast R-CNN detector inside a single unified network.
components: Region Proposal Network implemented as an n x n convolution followed by sibling 1 x 1 box-regression and box-classification layers
anchor boxes: 3 scales x 3 aspect ratios (k = 9) used as translation-invariant regression references
multi-task loss over anchor classification and box regression with smooth L1
image-centric sampling of 256 anchors per mini-batch with up to 1:1 positive/negative ratio
4-step alternating training to learn shared convolutional features between RPN and Fast R-CNN
non-maximum suppression (IoU 0.7) to prune redundant proposals before detection

evidence.quote: we introduce novel Region Proposal Networks (RPNs) that share convolutional layers with state-of-the-art object detection networks
The entire system is a single, unified network for object detection (Figure 2).
By default we use 3 scales and 3 aspect ratios, yielding k = 9 anchors at each sliding position.
In this paper, we adopt a pragmatic 4-step training algorithm to learn shared features via alternating optimization.
we adopt non-maximum suppression (NMS) on the proposal regions based on their cls scores.

experiments.summary: The method is evaluated on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 and MS COCO against Selective Search and EdgeBoxes proposals under Fast R-CNN, with ablations over shared vs. unshared features, proposal counts, cls/reg outputs, anchor settings and loss weight, plus a one-stage vs. two-stage comparison and timing on a K40 GPU.

evidence.quote: RPN with Fast R-CNN achieves competitive results, with an mAP of 59.9% while using up to 300 proposals
Using the ZF model, the one-stage system has an mAP of 53.9%.
Using the COCO trainval set to train, Faster RCNN has 42.7% mAP@0.5 and 21.9% mAP@[.5, .95] on the COCO test-dev set.

limitations.summary: The unified system is near real-time rather than truly real-time (198 ms / 5 fps with VGG-16), single-scale testing with a total stride of 16 limits localization precision, and the two-stage cascade still processes more work than a one-stage alternative.
items: With the very deep VGG-16 model the full pipeline runs at 5 fps (198 ms per image), so it is only near real-time.
The 16-pixel total stride on re-scaled images may limit accuracy; a smaller stride could improve results.
Multi-scale feature extraction at test time would raise accuracy but is rejected because it lacks a good speed-accuracy trade-off.
The two-stage design retains a per-region second stage, and the one-stage comparison runs slower mainly because of its far larger proposal count.

evidence.quote: Even such a large stride provides good results, though accuracy may be further improved with a smaller stride.
Multi-scale feature extraction (using an image pyramid) may improve accuracy but does not exhibit a good speed-accuracy trade-off [2].
We also note that the onestage system is slower as it has considerably more proposals to process.

futureDirections.direction: Develop an exact (non-approximate) joint-training solver that differentiates through RoI pooling with respect to predicted box coordinates, using an RoI warping layer.
futureDirections.quote: a solution can be given by an “RoI warping” layer as developed in [15], which is beyond the scope of this paper.

futureDirections.direction: Reduce the feature stride (e.g. by predicting on finer-resolution maps) to gain further detection accuracy.
futureDirections.quote: accuracy may be further improved with a smaller stride.

equations.name: RPN multi-task loss
equations.expr: L({pi},{ti}) = (1/Ncls) sum_i Lcls(pi,p*i) + lambda (1/Nreg) sum_i p*i Lreg(ti,t*i)

applications.detail: The detection system was adopted in commercial products such as Pinterest, where user engagement improvements were reported.
applications.quote: at Pinterests [17], with user engagement improvements reported.

applications.detail: RPN and Faster R-CNN formed the basis of 1st-place entries in ILSVRC 2015 detection/localization and COCO 2015 detection/segmentation tracks.
applications.quote: In ILSVRC and COCO 2015 competitions, Faster R-CNN and RPN are the foundations of the 1st-place winning entries in several tracks.

deploymentClaims: 5 fps including all steps on a GPU for the VGG-16 model (Abstract).
Total system time of 198 ms per image with VGG-16 for both proposal and detection (Sec 4.1).
17 fps frame rate with the ZF net (Sec 4.1).
The shared RPN adds only about 10 ms per image for proposals.

evidence.quote: For the very deep VGG-16 model [3], our detection system has a frame rate of 5fps (including all steps) on a GPU
With the convolutional features shared, the RPN alone only takes 10ms computing the additional layers.
Our system has a frame-rate of 17 fps with the ZF net.
